about: the polish round of Skerrow's places
reply: {"say":"Trimmed all eight descriptions to fit within seventy words while keeping every fact, sense, bracket topic and exit hint intact.","places":[{"id":"loc_skerrow_silver_grove","day":"Birches with bark gone silver-white stand close together, out of the wind, moss soft underfoot. Shells and scraps of cloth hang from the branches, ticking and chiming when the air moves. A turf hut with a crooked chimney sits among the trees. The cliff path runs south, the heights climb north to the barrow of [Old Skarth], and a track crosses east to the headland.","night":"The birches glimmer as if they held a little of the day back. The shells chime in the dark, very softly, and a thread of smoke smells of thyme from the hut among the trees. South is the cliff path, north the barrow, east the headland."},{"id":"loc_skerrow_headland","day":"The island ends here in a blunt headland, sea on three sides, a squat stone tower on top: the [beacon]. Its lamp stands cold behind green glass; wind whistles through the empty gallery. Below, a lean-to store shed has lost half its roof, and it reeks of fish oil. A track runs south to the hamlet, west to the grove; north a ruined tower stands alone.","night":"The beacon tower is a black tooth against the stars, its lamp as dark as the rest of the island. The sea booms on three sides. Tracks go south to the hamlet and west to the grove; north, the ruined tower is only a darker shape."},{"id":"loc_skerrow_mage_tower","day":"Half a tower of black stone stands on the last rise of Skerrow, its top storeys long fallen into the sea. Stairs climb round the wall to nowhere, and at the floor's centre stands the [waystone], a ring of black stone taller than a man. The air hums like a struck glass that never stops. A study of books, a lamp and a narrow cot sits within; south goes down to the headland.","night":"A single lamp burns among the books, and the runes on the [waystone] catch its light and seem to move. The hum in the air is louder in the dark. The way out is south, down to the headland."},{"id":"loc_skerrow_harbour","day":"A curved wall of piled stone keeps the sea from a harbour no bigger than a barn floor. Brannoc's boat, the Kittiwake, lies on the slip, mast bare, nets drying from every post. It smells of fish, wet rope and woodsmoke. Steps go north to the green; west, rocks lead back to the [Tidepools], and a low door by the slip opens into a cottage.","night":"Water slaps against the harbour wall in the dark, nets hanging from their posts like ghosts. The Kittiwake is a black shape on the slip. A line of firelight shows under the cottage door by the slip; steps go up north to the green."},{"id":"loc_skerrow_green","day":"A dozen stone cottages with turf roofs stand round wind-flattened grass and a squat well. Hens pick about your feet, and somewhere a door bangs in the wind, over and over. The lit door of the Salt Kettle shows on the east side. Steps lead south to the harbour, a track climbs north to the headland and the [beacon], and west the cliff path runs along the sea.","night":"The cottages are dark humps against a darker sky, and the wind hums in the well chain. Only the Salt Kettle, on the east side, still shows a light. Steps go south to the harbour, a track north to the headland, and the cliff path west."},{"id":"loc_skerrow_salt_kettle","day":"The inn is one long, smoky room under black beams, fire at one end, a barrel of ale at the other. It smells of fish stew, tallow and wet wool drying. A ship's figurehead, a woman with a chipped nose, watches the door from the corner; they say she came off the last ship that broke here before the [Grey Gull]. The door west goes out to the green.","night":"The fire is banked and the benches mostly empty. The figurehead in the corner holds a candle stub, wax run down her wooden arm. You can hear the wind trying the shutters. The door west goes out to the green."},{"id":"loc_skerrow_wreck_strand","day":"You stand on black shingle where the sea throws up what is left of the [Grey Gull]: a broken mast, a spill of wet rope, a cask rolling in the shallows. The stones clatter and hiss with every wave, and the air tastes of salt and tar. Gulls quarrel over something you would rather not look at. North, a path climbs the cliff; east, rocks give way to the [Tidepools].","night":"The strand is black on black, the sea a roar felt through your boots. Now and then the wreck of the [Grey Gull] knocks against the rocks like someone asking to be let in. There is no light anywhere on the island. A path climbs north, and the rocks run east."},{"id":"loc_skerrow_cliff_path","day":"A sheep track runs along the cliff top between thrift and sea campion. The wind comes straight off the Glass Sea and leans on you like a hand, and far below the waves boom in the caves. South, it drops to the [Wreck Strand]. Inland it climbs north towards a stand of pale trees, and east it runs down to the hamlet.","night":"The path is a pale thread along the edge of nothing. You hear the sea below more than you see it, a slow boom and suck in the caves. South is the strand; north the path climbs to the trees, east it goes down to the hamlet."}]}
